title: Intelligent Healthcare: A Systematic Review of Digital Twins in Healthcare Systems
content: Digital twins (DTs) have emerged as a transformative technology across various industries, and their potential in healthcare is garnering significant attention. DTs represent digital replicas of physical objects, systems, processes, and environments, offering unprecedented opportunities for personalized, precision, and intelligent healthcare. This paper systematically reviews the current applications of DTs in healthcare, focusing on how these technologies can enhance healthcare, improve patient and provider experiences, and deliver intelligent and personalized care. By leveraging immersive virtual worlds, healthcare practitioners can simulate complex medical situations, refine treatment strategies, and engage patients in more tailored, interactive ways. However, the integration of DTs into healthcare systems also presents technical, regulatory, and ethical challenges, such as data privacy concerns, the need for standardized protocols, and issues of accessibility. Addressing these challenges is crucial for the successful adoption and implementation of DTs in healthcare. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the transformative potential of DTs in intelligent healthcare, while also highlighting the need for continued research and development in this rapidly evolving field. Through this systematic review, we seek to encourage further innovation and collaboration, paving the way for a future where DTs play a central role in intelligent healthcare delivery.
